harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (standbys), with all replication traffic carried over TLS and mutual-cert authentication enforced via a cluster-dedicated CA. Verified live data replication, rejection of a cert not issued by the CA, and full recovery of all three nodes after sequential restarts with proven boot-identity changes.
actions_performed: Installed PostgreSQL 16 on node1, node2, node3
Generated a dedicated CA on node1 (/etc/postgresql-ca/ca.key+ca.crt) and issued CA-signed server certs (CN=node1/node2/node3) plus a client cert (CN=replicator) for mutual TLS

Distributed CA cert, server certs/keys, and replicator client cert/key to /etc/postgresql/16/main/tls on each node (outside the data directory, owned by postgres, 600 perms on keys) via secret_env-passed base64
Configured postgresql.conf on all nodes: listen_addresses='*', ssl=on with CA-signed cert/key/ca file paths, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on
Configured pg_hba.conf on all nodes to require hostssl + cert clientcert=verify-full for replication connections restricted to the cluster subnet, removing the prior scram-sha-256 replication rules
Created the REPLICATION role 'replicator' on node1
Created physical replication slots node2_slot/node3_slot on node1 to guard against WAL recycling
Bootstrapped node2 and node3 via pg_basebackup over sslmode=verify-full using the replicator client cert, with -R to auto-generate primary_conninfo/standby.signal
Diagnosed and fixed a key/cert mismatch on node3 (caused by an earlier base64 copy error) by restoring the correct server.key and replicator.key, verified via matching RSA modulus
Started both standbys and confirmed pg_stat_replication on node1 shows node2 and node3 streaming with ssl=t and client_dn=/CN=replicator
Verified live replication by inserting rows on node1 and confirming visibility on node2 and node3, then cleaned up test tables
Proved CA enforcement: a locally-generated self-signed cert with CN=replicator was rejected by node1 with 'SSL error: tlsv1 alert unknown ca'
Captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, service state, recovery state, replication state) on all three nodes
Restarted node2, then node3, then node1 (primary) one at a time via 'shutdown -r now', polled until each came back, and proved each node's /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id changed
After each restart, verified PostgreSQL was active, standbys resumed streaming over TLS with client_dn=/CN=replicator, and re-verified end-to-end data replication after all three nodes were back up

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication with node1 as writable primary, node2/node3 as standbys
evidence.summary: replicator role created on node1; node2/node3 bootstrapped via pg_basebackup with -R; both show pg_is_in_recovery=t and appear in pg_stat_replication as 'streaming'; an inserted row on node1 was visible on both standbys

evidence.requirement: CA created for the cluster and used to sign server/client certificates
evidence.summary: openssl req -x509 created ca.key/ca.crt on node1; per-node server certs (CN=node1/node2/node3) and a replicator client cert were all signed by this CA (CAcreateserial)

postgresql.conf ssl=on with CA-signed cert/key on all nodes; SHOW ssl returns 'on'; pg_stat_replication joined with pg_stat_ssl shows ssl=t and cipher TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 for both standby connections, including after the primary's restart

evidence.requirement: Replication connections accepted only from peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf requires hostssl+cert clientcert=verify-full for replication; legitimate connections show client_dn=/CN=replicator; a locally generated self-signed cert (not CA-issued) was rejected by node1 with 'SSL error: tlsv1 alert unknown ca'

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id dfeb3b70...; reboot acknowledged then connection dropped; post-reboot boot_id e4d99bb9... (changed); postgresql active, not in recovery, ssl=on, both standbys reconnected streaming over TLS

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a0c36ad2...; reboot acknowledged then connection reset; post-reboot boot_id d9690708... (changed); postgresql active, still in recovery, small replay lag, node1 shows node2 streaming again over TLS

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e8afb731...; reboot acknowledged then connection timeout; post-reboot boot_id cd39558c... (changed); postgresql active, still in recovery, small replay lag, node1 shows node3 streaming again over TLS

evidence.requirement: Post-restart data/cluster health verified end-to-end across all three nodes
evidence.summary: After all three nodes were restarted, a new row inserted on node1 was confirmed present on both node2 and node3, then the test table was dropped

attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (standbys), with all replication traffic carried over TLS and mutual-cert authentication enforced via a cluster-dedicated CA. Verified live data replication, rejection of a cert not issued by the CA, and full recovery of all three nodes after sequential restarts with proven boot-identity changes.
